definitions.explanation: The main woody stem of a tree that supports branches and leaves.

examples.japanese: この{木|き}は{幹|みき}が{太|ふと}い。
examples.english: This tree has a thick trunk.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちが{木|き}の{幹|みき}に{登|のぼ}っている。
examples.english: Children are climbing the tree trunk.

examples.japanese: {幹|みき}に{年輪|ねんりん}が{刻|きざ}まれている。
examples.english: Annual rings are carved into the trunk.

notes:
{幹|みき} refers to tree trunks.

Common expressions:
- {木|き}の{幹|みき} (tree trunk)
- {幹|みき}が{太|ふと}い (has a thick trunk)
- {幹|みき}を{切|き}る (to cut the trunk)

Related parts of trees:
- {枝|えだ} (branch)
- {根|ね} (root)
- {葉|は} (leaf)
- {樹皮|じゅひ} (bark)

Note:
{幹|みき} is distinct from the on'yomi {幹|かん} used in compound words like {幹線|かんせん} (main line), {幹部|かんぶ} (executive), and {幹事|かんじ} (organizer).
